skills.name: Describe the chemical properties of sulphur dioxide

note.text:
Sulphur dioxide is an acidic oxide, a reducing agent and a bleaching agent.
• Acidic oxide: SO2 + H2O → H2SO3 (sulphurous acid), which turns blue litmus red. With alkalis it gives sulphites: SO2 + 2NaOH → Na2SO3 + H2O.
• Reducing agent: it decolourises acidified potassium manganate(VII) (purple to colourless) and turns acidified potassium dichromate(VI) from orange to green. It also decolourises bromine water.
• Bleaching agent: it bleaches by reduction, so the bleaching is temporary; the colour slowly returns as air oxidises the material. Chlorine bleaches by oxidation and is permanent.
• As an oxidising agent with a stronger reducing agent: SO2 + 2H2S → 3S + 2H2O, giving a yellow deposit of sulphur.
In the air, SO2 is oxidised to SO3 and dissolves in rain as sulphuric acid: this is acid rain.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to describe sulphur dioxide as an acidic oxide, a reducing agent, a bleach and sometimes an oxidising agent.
Builds on: Lesson {3} (preparing {formula('SO2')}) and Form Three acids, bases and redox.
Leads to: Lesson {8} (sulphuric acid) and the problem of acid rain.

sections.heading: An acidic oxide and a reducing agent
sections.text:
Sulphur dioxide is the oxide of a non-metal, so it is acidic.
• With water: {formula('SO2')} + {formula('H2O')} → {formula('H2SO3')}, sulphurous acid, which turns blue litmus red.
• With an alkali: {formula('SO2')} + {2}{formula('NaOH')} → {formula('Na2SO3')} + {formula('H2O')}, giving a sulphite.
It is also a good reducing agent, and the colour changes are used as tests:
• acidified potassium manganate(VII): purple → colourless;
• acidified potassium dichromate(VI): orange → green;
• bromine water: brown → colourless.
In each case the {formula('SO2')} is itself oxidised to a sulphate.

sections.heading: Bleaching, oxidising and acid rain
sections.text:
Sulphur dioxide bleaches moist coloured materials such as flowers, straw, wool and paper. It does so by REDUCTION, so oxygen in the air slowly turns the colour back: the bleaching is temporary. Chlorine bleaches by oxidation, and that bleaching is permanent.
With a stronger reducing agent, {formula('SO2')} is itself the oxidising agent:
{formula('SO2')} + {2}{formula('H2S')} → {3}S + {2}{formula('H2O')}, seen as a pale yellow deposit of sulphur.
In the air, sulphur dioxide from burning coal and oil is oxidised and dissolves in rain as sulphuric acid. This acid rain damages buildings, kills fish in lakes and harms crops.

key_words.meaning: an oxide that gives an acid with water and a salt with an alkali
a substance that removes oxygen from, or gives electrons to, another
a bleach whose effect is slowly reversed by air
rain made acidic by dissolved oxides of sulphur and nitrogen

mistake.wrong: sulphur dioxide dissolves in water to give sulphuric acid
mistake.why: Sulphuric acid, {formula('H2SO4')}, comes from sulphur TRIoxide, {formula('SO3')}.

worked_example.problem: Explain, with an equation, what is seen when sulphur dioxide is bubbled through acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution.
steps: Acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution is purple.
Sulphur dioxide is a reducing agent, so it reduces the manganate(VII) ion.
The purple colour disappears and the solution becomes colourless.
The {formula('SO2')} is itself oxidised to sulphate: it gains oxygen from the oxidising agent.
worked_example.answer: the purple colour disappears, because {formula('SO2')} reduces the manganate(VII)

cards.idea: {formula('SO2')} bleaches by reduction, so the bleaching is temporary.
example: the colour returns as air oxidises the material again

pick.q: A red flower is held in moist sulphur dioxide and loses its colour. It is then left in the air for some days. What happens?
pick.r: The colour slowly returns, because the bleaching by {formula('SO2')} is temporary
w: The flower stays white for ever
e: Permanent bleaching is what chlorine does, by oxidation.
Blackening is what concentrated sulphuric acid does to sugar, by dehydration.
The change back takes days, because oxidation by air is slow.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} bleaches by reduction, and oxygen in the air slowly reverses it.

pick.q: Why must the material be moist for sulphur dioxide to bleach it?
pick.r: The gas must dissolve in the water to act on the colouring matter
w: Water is what does the bleaching
The water washes the colour away
e: Water alone does not remove the colour of a flower.
Nothing catches fire in this test.
Washing is not the effect: the colour is removed chemically, and later returns.
pick.y: Moisture lets the gas form sulphurous acid at the surface, and that is the reducing agent.

pick.q: Which bleach is used for cotton cloth, and why not sulphur dioxide?
pick.r: Chlorine or a chlorine compound, because its bleaching is permanent
w: Sulphur dioxide, because it is cheaper
Sulphur dioxide, because it is permanent
e: Cheapness does not help if the colour returns.
Cotton is bleached in large amounts in industry.
Bleaching by {formula('SO2')} is temporary, not permanent.
pick.y: Chlorine bleaches by oxidation, which the air cannot reverse; sulphur dioxide bleaches by reduction.

pick.q: Why is sulphur dioxide still used to bleach straw, wool and paper?
pick.r: Chlorine would attack and weaken those materials, while sulphur dioxide does not
w: It is the only bleach that works on them
Its bleaching lasts longer than chlorine's
e: Other bleaches exist, but they damage these materials.
Bleaching does not strengthen a material.
Its bleaching lasts a shorter time, not longer.
pick.y: A gentle reducing bleach is chosen where an oxidising bleach would damage the fibres.

pick.q: What does sulphur dioxide form when it dissolves in water?
pick.r: Sulphurous acid, {formula('H2SO3')}
e: Sulphuric acid comes from sulphur TRIoxide dissolving in water.
Hydrogen sulphide is a different compound, made from a sulphide and an acid.
The solution turns blue litmus red, so it is acidic.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} + {formula('H2O')} → {formula('H2SO3')}: an acidic oxide gives an acid.

pick.q: What happens when sulphur dioxide is bubbled into acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution?
pick.r: The purple colour disappears, because the {formula('SO2')} reduces it
w: The solution turns a deeper purple
e: Reduction removes the purple colour; it does not deepen it.
Brown is what happens with bromine water, not with manganate(VII).
The colour change is clear and is used as a test.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} is a reducing agent: it is itself oxidised to a sulphate while the purple ion is reduced.

pick.q: Why is the bleaching by sulphur dioxide called temporary?
pick.r: The colour slowly returns as air oxidises the bleached material
w: The bleaching only works in the dark
The material is destroyed rather than bleached
e: Light is not what undoes it; oxygen from the air is.
The material is not destroyed; its colour is removed and then returns.
It works on wool, silk, straw and paper as well.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} bleaches by reduction, and oxygen in the air slowly reverses the change.

pick.q: How does bleaching by sulphur dioxide differ from bleaching by chlorine?
pick.r: Sulphur dioxide bleaches by reduction; chlorine bleaches by oxidation
w: Sulphur dioxide bleaches by oxidation and chlorine by reduction
e: Chlorine bleaches by oxidation, but sulphur dioxide does not.
Chlorine is an oxidising bleach, not a reducing one.
It is the other way round.
pick.y: That is why the bleaching by {formula('SO2')} is temporary and that by chlorine is permanent.

pick.q: Sulphur dioxide is bubbled through hydrogen sulphide. What is seen?
pick.r: A yellow deposit of sulphur forms
e: No white precipitate is formed in this reaction.
No blue colour appears.
A pale yellow solid appears clearly.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} + {2}{formula('H2S')} → {3}S + {2}{formula('H2O')}: here {formula('SO2')} acts as the oxidising agent.

pick.q: Which gas is mainly responsible for acid rain from burning coal?
pick.r: Sulphur dioxide
e: Carbon dioxide makes rain only very slightly acidic; it is not the main cause of acid rain.
Nitrogen in the air is unreactive and does not itself cause acid rain.
Oxygen is neutral.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} from the sulphur in coal dissolves in rain and is oxidised to sulphuric acid.

questions.prompt: What volume of sulphur dioxide, in dm³ at s.t.p., is given off when {n} mol of sodium sulphite reacts completely with dilute hydrochloric acid?

misconceptions.explain: The equation gives {1} mol of {formula('SO2')} for each {1} mol of sulphite, not {2}.
Multiply the moles by {22.4} dm³/mol; do not divide.

solution: {1} mol of sulphite gives {1} mol of {formula('SO2')}, so {n} mol gives {n} mol.
At s.t.p. {1} mol of any gas is {22.4} dm³, so the volume is {n} × {22.4} = {answer} dm³.
